title: Jean du Bellay (London) to Montmorency, 1529, BnF fr. 3077 and fr. 3078 (catalogue item 4; the 1528 letter split off to dubellay1528)

steps.what: Gallica IIIF for fr. 3077/3078; connections dropped and 429s, only fr. 3078 pp. 21-27, 31-32 (later 113-117, 133-134) at full size.
Dated the notice items against Le Grand 1688, L&P IV and Bourrilly 1905: all five catalogue letters are in print in clear.
Re-derived the key from the 22 June letter's interlinear decipherment, extending Tomokiyo's table (B = o, word signs bien, fault, paix).
Read the 16 June 1529 block (p. 21) in stretches, about 60 % of signs.
Key read the opening of the 17 Oct letter from the leaf, matching Le Grand; boxed cross = le Cardinal.
DECODE with login cookie: record pages and images for R3688-R3693, R4229; R9467 (Friedmann key) has no image attached; no DOC transcriptions on any record. Gallica IIIF/SRU 403 (Cloudflare).
DECODE harvest swept for du Bellay/Bayonne, fr. 3040/3077/3078/3005, Clair. 328-333, NAF 4206: R4229 fr. 3040 f. 68 = 30 June 1529, printed by Le Grand III 333 ff., L&P IV 5742.
p. 21 cipher block re-transcribed sign by sign from DECODE's high-resolution crop (194 signs, p21_signs.txt).

Deciphered lines 0-6 of p. 21 with the re-derived key plus Tomokiyo's table: 'si vous trouvez bon l'advis que piecza vous ay envoe de faire semblant que madame ne fust allee pour conclure et qu'estant la [?] luy ayt par importunite [R] envoye querir pouoir il ne [?] faudroyt oublier a le faire dater de ce temps la et du lieu'; fixed x-over-x = l, bracket = q, triangle-on-cross = i, diamond family m/t/n.

Scheurer t. I (1969) found through Google Books snippets: no. 12 p. 41 prints the 16 June block in clear, agreeing with the leaf reading; supplies vous, faict, madame Marguerite and 'ou sera le Roy'. Pp. 111-112 print the 22 Oct 1529 opening called undeciphered by Le Grand and L&P.
Leaf reading compared word by word with Scheurer p. 41: all words agree; signs give 'estant la' where the snippet has 'ostant'; 164 of 167 signs counted as valued (98.2%; recounted below).

Recount for the write-up: the measure had skipped line 6 (it opens with '=', read as a comment marker). Lines labelled L0-L7; 194 signs, 191 with an established value (98.5%). Before Scheurer, lines 0-6 (181 signs) had all but four values (null, vous, faict, boxed cross).

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): fr. 3077 no. 23 (28 Oct 1528) is in du Bellay's first cipher (Bourrilly 1905; Lasry 2022) and is now dubellay1528; this entry keeps Bayonne's cipher of 1529. Credits for Bourrilly (1528 key) and Lasry (1528 cipher) moved to dubellay1528.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): 16 June: p21_signs.txt + texts/16jun1529_decryption.md (copied from p21_transcription.md/NOTES); 22 June, 30 June, 17 Oct: Le Grand 1688 OCR in ref/; 17 Oct partial sign transcription copied from NOTES section 5; 22 Oct: Scheurer 1969 linked; key_file key_p21.tsv. No ciphertext transcription for 22 June, 30 June, 22 Oct.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): for 22 Oct 1529 the repository has only Le Grand's clear part; the ciphered opening is Scheurer's (snippets). Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (in print).

fr. 3005 identified as Gallica ark btv1b90599952 (Tomokiyo's francis.htm link); folio numbers read on the canvas corners (259 = f. 165r, 260 = f. 165v, 261 = f. 166r); full-resolution leaves fetched through openapi.bnf.fr IIIF. Neighbouring leaves (canvases 255-266) checked: no decipherment.

Ciphered opening (34 + 35 + 5 lines) read sign by sign on native-resolution strips (research/reading_audit/b26_strips.py) with key_p21.tsv and Tomokiyo's table; value transcription texts/22oct1529_transcription.txt; sign values beyond the key in texts/22oct1529_corrections.tsv (adopted: cup = a, barred cup = s, ƕ = f, tall ϙ = m, barred triangle = l, x on a stem = e; confirmed R = faict, V = bien, 4 = madame; sense only, flagged: ꝑ and ℋ = the two Kings).

First lines agree with Scheurer's snippets word for word (la ou je vouldroye ... seul feal; maint tour de corde); 'si le roy et madame ne l'aydent' matches Le Grand's 17 Oct letter. Reading body scored (b17_score.py, fr): 0.513 (20/39), explicit holes 0.692 (27/39); the last two paragraphs do not build sentences. Kept decoded, not read; 10 letters rest on look-alike alternates.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: Every 1529 cipher passage of the catalogue item is printed in clear (Le Grand 1688), and so are the two by-products once thought unread: the 16 June 1529 block (Scheurer 1969 no. 12 p. 41) and the 22 Oct 1529 opening (Scheurer pp. 111-112). The project re-derived the key from the 22 June interlinear and deciphered lines 0-6 of the 16 June block from the leaf before finding Scheurer, who confirmed it.
outcome.notes: 16 June 1529 block: 194 signs, 191 with an established value (98.5%), all plaintext words read and matching Scheurer; three isolated signs in line 7 unexplained. Catalogue item found already solved; R4229 (30 June 1529) also in print. Open question: the boxed cross is 'madame Marguerite' on p. 21 (Scheurer) but lined up with 'le Cardinal' on p. 113; one sign or two not settled. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the 22 Oct 1529 entry is decoded, not read (its ciphered opening is not in the repository); class kept: Scheurer prints it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: p21_signs.txt (191 of 194 signs with an established value; the 16 June block only)

texts.label: 16 June 1529, fr. 3078 p. 21 (R3688)
texts.summary: Jean du Bellay, bishop of Bayonne, to Montmorency from London, 16 June 1529: the clear text is about the bishopric he hoped for and a move against him; the cipher block advises, if his earlier counsel is followed (to pretend that Madame had not gone to conclude, and that Margaret of Austria, being there, had by importunity had a power sent for), to have that power dated from that time and from the place where the King will be (the Cambrai peace negotiation). Deciphered here from the leaf; Scheurer (1969) prints the same text.
texts.note: Scheurer's edition (1969) is a modern publication, linked (Google Books snippet view), not copied.

texts.label: 22 June 1529, fr. 3078 pp. 25-27 (Le Grand III pp. 327-332)
texts.summary: Du Bellay to Montmorency from London, 22 June 1529, with the Court decipherer's word-by-word interlinear reading on the leaf; printed by Le Grand, Histoire du divorce III (1688) pp. 327-332, and used here to re-derive the key.
texts.note: Decryption = OCR of Le Grand 1688 (the letter is at pp. 327-332 of the file, which holds other letters too). No transcription of the ciphertext (signs were only aligned with the interlinear to derive the key): project work.

texts.label: 17 Oct 1529, fr. 3078 pp. 113-117 (Le Grand III pp. 369-375)
texts.summary: Du Bellay to Montmorency from London, 17 Oct 1529, on Wolsey's fall ("j'ay esté voir le Cardinal en ses ennuis"); printed by Le Grand III pp. 369-375 from a deciphered copy (Clair. 330 f. 71); the first cipher lines were deciphered here on the leaf as a check of the key.
texts.note: Transcription covers only the first cipher lines of p. 113 (NOTES section 5); the rest of the four pages is not transcribed (project work). Decryption = OCR of Le Grand 1688, pp. 369-375 of the file.

texts.label: 30 June 1529, fr. 3040 f. 68 (R4229; Le Grand III pp. 333 ff.)
texts.summary: Du Bellay to Montmorency from London, last day of June 1529, about two of its four pages in cipher; printed in clear by Le Grand III pp. 333 ff. and calendared in L&P IV 5742; Tomokiyo's Clair. 329 f. 139 is the deciphered copy.
texts.note: Decryption = OCR of Le Grand 1688, from p. 333 of the file. No transcription of the ciphertext (identified, not transcribed): project work.

Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b26): the leaf found on Gallica (fr. 3005 = btv1b90599952, canvases 259-261 = ff. 165r-166r; 74 cipher lines, the signed original) and read sign by sign with the 1529 key: texts/22oct1529_reading.md (partial reading), transcription, corrections, log. The first half builds sentences and agrees with Scheurer's snippets (the seal taken, the inventory, the charges: Ferrara league, bond, war on the Emperor; 'ilz pretendent luy faict perdre la teste'); f. 165v ll. 21-35 and f. 166r ll. 1-5 keep unread stretches and five unidentified word-sign places. Score 0.51 (explicit holes 0.69): below the bar. Blocker: needs-physical-access (Scheurer t. I 1969 prints the whole opening, snippet view only; Friedmann's key NAF 4206 no. 5 not imaged).
texts.label: 22 Oct 1529, fr. 3005 f. 165 (Scheurer t. I pp. 111-112; Le Grand III pp. 377-379)
texts.summary: Du Bellay to Montmorency from London, 22 Oct 1529: the ciphered opening, on granting the cardinal of York's request made through his Italian servant (Agostino, Wolsey's physician), had no known decipherment for Le Grand 1688, Brewer and Tomokiyo, but its decipherment is printed by Scheurer (1969); the clear part, on the Legate being turned out of his house, is in Le Grand III pp. 377-379.
